notes.text: Man — A weak creature, and withal corrupt and sinful, and of that sex by which sin and all other calamity was brought into the world.

Flower — The flower is fading, and all its beauty soon withers and is gone. The shadow is fleeting, and its very being will soon be lost in the shadows of night. Of neither do we make any account, in neither do we put any confidence.
Not one — No man. This is the prerogative of thy grace, which therefore I humbly implore.
Determined — Limited to a certain period. With thee - In thy power and disposal. Thou hast appointed a certain end of his days, beyond which he cannot prolong his life.

Turn — Withdraw thine afflicting hand from him, that he may have some present ease. 'Till - He come to the period of his life, which thou hast allotted to him, as a man appoints a set time to an hired servant.
Die — To outward appearance.
Scent — By means of water. Scent or smell, is figuratively ascribed to a tree.

Man — Two words are here used for man. Geber, a mighty man, tho' mighty, dies. Adam, a man of earth, returns to it. Before death, he is dying daily, continually wasting away. In death, he giveth up the ghost, the spirit returns to God that gave it. After death, where is he? Not where he was: his place knows him no more. But is he nowhere? Yes, he is gone to the world of spirits, gone into eternity, gone, never to return to this world!

As — So it is with man. Or thus, as when the waters fail from the sea, when the sea forsakes the place into which it used to flow, the river which was fed by it, decayeth and drieth up without all hopes of recovery.
Lieth — In his bed, the grave. 'Till - Until the time of the general resurrection, when these visible heavens shall pass away.

The grave — The grave is not only a resting-place, but an hiding-place to the children of God. He hides them in the grave, as we hide our treasure in a place of secrecy and safety. Hide me there, not only from the storms of this life, but for the glory of a better. Until thy wrath be past - As long as our bodies lie in the grave, there are some fruits of God's wrath against sin: until the set time comes, for their being remembered, as Noah was remembered in the ark, Gen. viii, 1. Our bodies shall not be forgotten in the grave, there is a time set for their being inquired after.
Shall he live? — He shall not in this world. Therefore I will patiently wait 'till that change comes, which will put a period to my calamities.

glossa.text: « Man born of woman. » ((GREG.)) Here by the name of woman infirmity is designated, and the sense is: What has he of strength in himself, who is born of infirmity, who is both straitened unto life, and enlarged unto misery.

« Who cometh forth like a flower. » Because he shines in the flesh:

« He is crushed, » because he is brought back into dust and rottenness.

« And he fleeth as a shadow. » He compared man not to one merely fleeing, but to a shadow. For he who has not the warmth of the heart in the love of God, and yet does not hold the life which he loves, flees like a shadow.

« And never in the same state, » etc. ((Ibid.)) For he always fails from that very point whence he believes himself to advance into a span of life.
« And dost thou think it worthy over such a one, » etc. For God to open his eyes is to exercise judgments, and to see whom he strikes
« Who can make, » etc. For he who alone is clean of himself, etc., *as far as* he says that Christ alone was not born of unclean seed.

« Short are the days of man, » etc. ((Ibid.)), because with God even the things that slip away stand fast: he declares that the number of the months is with him. Or, in days the brevity of time, in months the multiplied spaces of days are designated: to man therefore the days are brief; but because our life is stretched out afterward, the number of our months is recorded to be with God.

« Thou hast appointed his bounds. » ((GREG. in Job. l. XII.)) For none of the things that come to pass for men in this world come to pass without the hidden judgment of God.

« Depart a little from him. » Withdraw, that is, now take away the scourges of the present life, and show the good things of eternal rest

« Until the desired come, » when he receives eternal rest as the recompense of his labor

« A tree hath hope. » etc. He hints that the human race is as it were despised, and how far insensible things themselves seem to go before it. Or according to the mystical sense: the tree is preferred to man, for here every carnal man is the man; the tree is taken as the just man, who, when in death he is afflicted with suffering, is recovered in the greenness of eternal life.

« And its branches sprout, » because out of the suffering of the just man the faithful receive the greenness of spiritual life.

« If its root grow old in the earth. » ((Ibid.)) The root of the just man is holy preaching, because from it he arises and in it he subsists: which among the hearts of earthly men is believed to be spent of all its strength: « And in the dust the trunk dieth, » because among the hands of persecutors his body is deprived of life.

« At the scent of water it shall spring up, » etc. Because through the breathing of the Spirit, in the hearts of the elect, by the example of his own work, he makes the seed of virtue.

 « And shall put forth foliage, » etc. For a cut trunk to make foliage, etc., *as far as* he made foliage, because the apostles who had withered grew green unto the faith as before.

« But when man shall be dead. » ((Ibid.)) But by that very loss of justice man dies, he is stripped of the garment of innocence granted in paradise, he is consumed, the destruction of the flesh following: « where then is he, » he who is not in his love, where « true being » is?
« As if the waters should depart from the sea. » The sea is the mind of man, etc., *as far as* we are now filled with the sweetness of prosperity.
« Until the heaven be worn away he shall not awake. » Because, unless the end of this world shall have come, the human race shall not awake from sleep.

« Who will grant me this. » Before the coming of the Mediator, knowing that he was to descend to hell, he asks there for the protection of his Creator.

« That thou appoint me a time wherein thou wilt remember me. » He asks for the coming of the Redeemer to the lower regions.

« Thinkest thou that a dead man again. » Just men are wont, etc., *as far as* that afterward he may strengthen the more.

« All the days. » He therefore who awaits his own change with so great desire, shows how certain he is concerning the resurrection.

notes.text: Ashamed — Of my confidence in thy promise. Deliver me - According to thy faithfulness and goodness.

glossa.text: *In thee, O Lord, have I hoped,* etc. ((ID.)) There is an eternal confusion, from which he asks to be delivered: and there is a temporal one, for an hour, namely the kind that profits.

*Make haste.* ((ID.)) In the things to be done, in the souls to be loosed and the like, that thou mayest rescue me on the third day and not defer it to the common resurrection; and that this may be, be thou to me a protector as great as it befits God to be. *Be thou to me.* He said: Give justice, etc., *as far as* he affirms the deliverance.

*Thou wilt bring out.* ((CASS.)) From death to the things above, so that the counsels of the Jews may be in vain. *Out of the snare which they have hidden.* ((AUG.)) The devil tempts by two gates, etc., *as far as* whence: *Thou wilt bring me out of the snare.*

notes.text: Arm yourselves with the same mind — Which will be armour of proof against all your enemies. For he that hath suffered in the flesh - That hath so suffered as to be thereby made inwardly and truly conformable to the sufferings of Christ. Hath ceased from sin - Is delivered from it.
That ye may no longer live in the flesh — Even in this mortal body. To the desires of men - Either your own or those of others. These are various; but the will of God is one.

Revellings, banquetings — Have these words any meaning now? They had, seventeen hundred years ago. Then the former meant, meetings to eat; meetings, the direct end of which was, to please the taste: the latter, meetings to drink: both of which Christians then ranked with abominable idolatries.
The same — As ye did once. Speaking evil of you - As proud, singular, silly, wicked and the like.
Who shall give account — Of this, as well as all their other ways. To him who is ready - So faith represents him now.

For to this end was the gospel preached — Ever since it was given to Adam. To them that are now dead - In their several generations. That they might be judged - That though they were judged. In the flesh according to the manner of men - With rash, unrighteous judgment. They might live according to the will and word of God, in the Spirit; the soul renewed after his image.

But the end of all things — And so of their wrongs, and your sufferings. Is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer - Temperance helps watchfulness, and both of them help prayer. Watch, that ye may pray; and pray, that ye may watch.

Love covereth a multitude of sins — Yea, "love covereth all things." He that loves another, covers his faults, how many soever they be. He turns away his own eyes from them; and, as far as is possible, hides them from others. And he continually prays that all the sinner's iniquities may be forgiven and his sins covered. Meantime the God of love measures to him with the same measure into his bosom.

glossa.text: *Because he that hath suffered. ((BEDA.))*. He who by the fear of the heavenly judgments extinguishes carnal concupiscences in his mind is already like to Christ crucified, being as it were dead to sins. He lives for the service of God alone.
*Blaspheming. ((ID.))* And if they blaspheme you as separated from their perfidy, yet, seeing in your conversation the works of justice and piety, they marvel, and in a manner venerate the faith.

*For this cause was the gospel preached also to the dead. ((BEDA.))* So great is God's care that we be mortified in the flesh, etc., *as far as* that their own reason may condemn the evils in the ungodly.

*Of all things.* Because he had said that the living and the dead were to be judged in the judgment, lest any should flatter himself concerning the remoteness of the judgment to come, he advisedly admonishes, because although the coming of the last crisis is uncertain, yet it is certain to all that we cannot long subsist in this life.

*Watch in prayers. ((BEDA.))* Let not the mind think anything beyond that alone which it prays for. When we stand to pray, let every carnal thought depart, let the sincere intention of the heart pray to God not with the sound of the voice, but with the sense of the mind.
*Having a continual charity. ((ID.))* He who through charity admonishes his neighbour, rebukes him, etc., *as far as* although in public it is not always, able to be shown.

notes.text: When the evening was come — That is, after three o'clock; the time from three to six they termed the evening. Mark xv, 42; Luke xxiii, 50; John xix, 38.

On the morrow, the day that followed the day of the preparation — The day of preparation was the day before the Sabbath, whereon they were to prepare for the celebration of it. The next day then was the Sabbath according to the Jews. But the evangelist seems to express it by this circumlocution, to show the Jewish Sabbath was then abolished.

That impostor said, while he was yet alive, After three days I will rise again — We do not find that he had ever said this to them, unless when he spoke of the temple of his body, John ii, 19, 21. And if they here refer to what he then said, how perverse and iniquitous was their construction on these words, when he was on his trial before the council? Chap. xxvi, 61. Then they seemed not to understand them!
Ye have a guard — Of your own, in the tower of Antonia, which was stationed there for the service of the temple.

They went and secured the sepulchre, sealing the stone, and setting a guard — They set Pilate's signet, or the public seal of the sanhedrim upon a fastening which they had put on the stone. And all this uncommon caution was overruled by the providence of God, to give the strongest proofs of Christ's ensuing resurrection; since there could be no room for the least suspicion of deceit, when it should be found, that his body was raised out of a new tomb, where there was no other corpse, and this tomb hewn out of a rock, the mouth of which was secured by a great stone, under a seal, and a guard of soldiers.

glossa.text: *A rich man.* Because none but a rich man could approach the governor, not that the evangelist commends riches. He was called also a decurion, because he was of the order of the curia and discharged the office of the curia, by this he could have the means, by this, that he was a disciple, he was worthy of this ministry. *He was a disciple of Jesus. He went to Pilate.* Although in secret, avoiding beforehand the enmities of the Jews, in this last office he cares nothing for them.

*In a clean linen cloth.* Mystically. He wraps Jesus in a clean linen cloth who receives him with a pure mind. Hence also the custom of the Church holds that the sacrifice of the altar be celebrated not upon silk, not upon dyed cloth, but upon pure linen.

*In his own new monument.* Because, if he were laid in a monument where another had been laid, another perhaps would be feigned to have risen again. In the rock, lest, if it had been built of many stones, he should be said to have been taken away by theft, the foundations of the tomb being undermined.

*And there were there.* While the other acquaintances of Jesus were returning to their own, the women alone, who loved more closely, were watching the service of the burial, awaiting what Jesus had promised: and therefore they are the first to see the resurrection.

*After three.* The whole from a part, of the sixth day, on which he was crucified, with its own night, for one day. The sabbath entire. The third day from its first part, that is, from the night, for the whole with its own daytime, and so there is a space of three days.
*They made the sepulchre sure.* Their diligence profited our faith. For the more it was guarded, the more is the power of the resurrection shown.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The stone is rolled; the tomb is sealed.
In the silence, we wait for you.
Job's question hangs in the dark: if we die, shall we live again?
Into your hand we commit our spirit.
The Sabbath rest covers the grave.
We wait, O Lord, for the morning.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The body is wrapped and laid in the rock-cut tomb; the great stone is rolled, the seal is set, the guards take their watch.
In the silence, we wait for you.
A mortal, born of woman, lies down and does not rise; if a tree is cut down there is hope, but who will answer for the dead?
In the silence, we wait for you.
You are our rock and our refuge; into your hand we commit our spirit, even here, even now.
In the silence, we wait for you.
The whole creation holds its breath through the long Sabbath dark; we wait for a morning that has not yet come.
In the silence, we wait for you. Amen.
